course_name_original: Diseño de Circuitos Electrónicos para Comunicaciones
course_name_en: Design of Electronic Circuits for Communications
prerequisites: Refreshed knowledge of undergraduate electronics courses.
Having taken 'Electrónica de Comunicaciones' (4th year elective) or reviewing its study material.
Reviewing contents of 'Fundamentos de Electrónica Analógica' (2nd year) related to communications electronics.

learning_outcomes.text: Design linear (Class A and Class B) broadband and narrowband power amplifier stages.
Design non-linear (Class D, Class E, and Class F) narrowband power amplifier stages.
Improve the performance of linear amplifiers using techniques such as Envelope Tracking and Doherty technique.
Design linear-behavior power amplifiers, based on high-performance non-linear amplifiers, using Envelope Elimination and Restoration techniques.
Design optoelectronic conversion subsystems and signal conditioning for optical receivers and transmitters.
Design electronic circuitry for the regeneration of digital signals distorted during transmission.
Design receivers and transmitters based on integrated circuits according to their band and operating characteristics.
Design transceivers for different bands, powers, and modulation types. Acquire criteria for selecting transceivers based on the application.
Design optical receivers and transmitters for both guided (optical fiber) and unguided communications.
Design Hubs, Switches, and Routers. Acquire criteria for selecting these devices based on the application.

syllabus_topics: Frequency synthesis: synthesizers based on PLLs and Direct Digital Synthesis (DDSs).
Communications power amplifiers: Linear and non-linear amplifiers (Class D, E, and F).
Techniques for improving the performance of linear power amplifiers.
Components and subsystems for optical receivers and transmitters.
Types, structure, and integrated circuits of receivers and transmitters.
Transceivers. Design examples with integrated transceivers.
Guided and unguided optical transmitters and receivers.
Types, structure, and dedicated integrated circuits of concentrators (hubs), switches, and routers.
assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, the theoretical block grade is (0.7 * EF1) + (0.2 * T) and the practical block grade is (0.1 * PL). The final grade is Theory + Practice. For the extraordinary call, the final grade is (0.7 * EF2) + (0.2 * T) + (0.1 * PL). For differentiated evaluation, the final grade is (0.8 * EF) + (0.2 * T). Grades obtained for Work (T) and Laboratory Practices (PL) are retained only for calls within the same academic year.
